meta.topic: ₹18,500 debit but e-commerce order remains pending

problem:
A customer of Northgate Retail pays Rs 18,500 for an order through the retailer's checkout. The bank account is debited, the payment gateway reports success, and the order remains pending: no confirmation, no dispatch, no delivery date. The customer contacts support, who can see the debit in the bank statement but cannot see the order, and the retailer cannot tell the customer whether the goods will arrive or the money will come back. The amount matters for the investigation: Rs 18,500 is well within the usual bank cap of around Rs 5 lakh for IMPS, and within the UPI limit of INR 5 lakh for specified categories, so the failure is not a limit breach. It is a state failure: the money moved, or appears to have moved, while the order state did not.

The learner must trace the payment through the gateway, the bank, the merchant callback and the order creation, and then decide between the two possible endings: fulfilment or refund. That decision cannot be made from the customer's statement alone, nor from the gateway's success alone. It needs the ledger entry, the gateway record, the callback delivery record and the order system state, all matched on the same reference. The case also tests the recovery discipline for the amount in question: a Rs 18,500 debit that is not matched to an order must be resolved through a controlled process with a reference the customer can quote, not through an informal promise that the money will come back.
solution:
Start by fixing the reference: take the payment reference from the customer's bank statement and the gateway transaction ID, and confirm they belong to the same payment. Then trace the four boundaries in order. First, the gateway: did it authorise and capture the payment, what response did it return, and what callback did it send? Second, the bank: does the ledger show a debit of Rs 18,500, on which rail, and with what status? The rail matters for the timeline: IMPS is instant and typically bank-capped around Rs 5 lakh, NEFT settles in half-hourly batches, RTGS settles individually in real time with a minimum of Rs 2 lakh, and UPI allows INR 5 lakh for specified categories, so a Rs 18,500 payment could have travelled on IMPS or UPI without breaching a limit, and the rail record shows whether settlement completed. Third, the merchant callback: was it delivered, did the endpoint acknowledge it, and does the dead-letter queue hold it? Fourth, the order system: was an order created, in what state, and is it linked to the payment reference?

Once the four boundaries are known, the decision follows the evidence. If the payment completed and the callback was lost, create the order from the payment record exactly once and confirm fulfilment to the customer with the order reference. If the payment did not complete, or the debit is provisional and will not settle, refund the Rs 18,500 through the controlled process with a refund reference, a date and a written confirmation. If the state is still uncertain after the trace, hold the payment in a controlled recovery state, tell the customer what is known, what is being checked and when the next update will come, and do not promise a date the bank cannot guarantee. Record every step against the same reference so the customer, support and finance all see one story.

decision.question: A customer pays Rs 18,500 at Northgate Retail. The bank account is debited and the gateway reports success, but the order remains pending with no confirmation or dispatch. Support can see the debit but cannot see the order. You are the business analyst asked to trace the payment and decide whether the customer gets fulfilment or a refund.

options.label: A
options.detail: Treat the gateway success as proof the order will be fulfilled and tell the customer to wait.

options.label: B
options.detail: Tell the customer the money will be refunded automatically and close the case.

options.label: C
options.detail: Trace the gateway, bank, merchant callback and order creation on the same reference, establish whether the payment completed, and then fulfil the order or refund through a controlled process with a reference.

options.label: D
options.detail: Ask the customer to pay again so the order can be created, and sort out the first debit later.

decisionRationale: Option C is correct because only a traced, evidenced decision can choose between fulfilment and refund, and either ending needs a controlled process with a reference. Option B promises a refund before knowing whether the payment completed. Option D takes a second Rs 18,500 before the first is resolved. Option A treats a gateway success as proof of an order that the order system never created.

steps.title: Capture the payment reference and gateway transaction ID and open the case
Trace the gateway record, response and callback delivery
Confirm the ledger debit of Rs 18,500, the rail and the settlement status
Check callback delivery, endpoint acknowledgement and dead-letter queue
Check the order system for an order linked to the payment reference
Decide fulfilment or refund on the evidence and record the decision
Confirm the outcome to the customer with the order or refund reference

happy: The customer receives one clear outcome: either the order is created and confirmed with an order reference and a delivery expectation, or the Rs 18,500 is refunded with a refund reference and a date. The payment, the callback, the ledger entry and the order are all linked on the same reference, and the case record shows the evidence the decision rested on.

negative.title: Gateway success but callback lost
negative.detail: The payment completed but the callback that creates the order never arrived. Create the order from the payment record exactly once and confirm fulfilment with the order reference.

negative.title: Debit provisional and payment not settled
negative.detail: The bank shows a debit but the rail record shows the payment did not complete. Refund through the controlled process with a refund reference and a written confirmation.

negative.title: Late success after a refund was promised
negative.detail: The payment completes after support has already told the customer a refund is coming. Cancel the refund, create the order, and tell the customer what changed and why, with the new reference.

negative.title: Duplicate charge on retry
negative.detail: The customer paid again while the first payment was unresolved. Reverse the duplicate exactly once through the controlled process and link both payments to the same case.

technical: Persist the payment reference, the gateway transaction ID, the correlation ID, the ledger entry reference, the callback delivery attempts and the order reference in one case record, so any team can follow the same payment. Log the rail and settlement status with the amount, currency and timestamp, and keep the customer's statement reference alongside the bank's records. Store the decision, the decision maker and the evidence relied on, and log the fulfilment or refund with its reference, date and operator. Never store full card or account credentials in the case record.

accounting: A Rs 18,500 debit with no order is a real financial break, not a display problem, so reconciliation must treat it as one: match every gateway payment to an order or a refund each day, and age unmatched items into a worklist with service levels and an owner. If the order is fulfilled, the merchant's revenue and the customer's payment reconcile on the same reference. If the money is refunded, the refund is a separate credit to the customer account with its own reference, reconciled separately from the original debit so finance can prove the customer is whole. Operations must be able to answer, for any unmatched debit, how old it is, who owns it, and what the next step is.

questions.question: Why is the gateway success alone not enough to promise fulfilment?
options: Gateway success may mean acceptance, while the order depends on callback delivery and order creation
questions.explanation: The gateway, the bank, the callback and the order system are separate boundaries, and success at one does not prove the others completed.

questions.question: Which rail facts are relevant to a Rs 18,500 payment in India?
options: RTGS minimum Rs 2 lakh means it could not have used RTGS; IMPS and UPI can carry it within their limits
questions.explanation: RTGS has a minimum of Rs 2 lakh, so a Rs 18,500 payment could not have used RTGS, while IMPS and UPI can carry it within their limits.

questions.question: What should support tell the customer while the outcome is still uncertain?
options: That the order is on its way
What is known, what is being checked and when the next update will come
That the money will be back tomorrow
questions.explanation: An honest holding message states what is known, what is being checked and when the next update will come, without promising a date the bank cannot guarantee.

questions.question: How should a refund be recorded?
options: As a separate credit with its own reference, reconciled separately from the original debit
questions.explanation: A refund is a separate credit with its own reference, reconciled separately from the original debit, so finance can prove the customer is whole.
